findings.message: The sitemap.xml table contains multiple unfilled placeholder tokens ([SITEMAP_URL_COUNT], [SITEMAP_LOC_ASSESSMENT], [SITEMAP_HAS_LASTMOD], [SITEMAP_LASTMOD_ASSESSMENT], [SITEMAP_HAS_CHANGEFREQ], [SITEMAP_CHANGEFREQ_ASSESSMENT], [SITEMAP_HAS_PRIORITY], [SITEMAP_PRIORITY_ASSESSMENT], [SITEMAP_GRADE]) that were never replaced with real audit data. These are leaked template-slot descriptors visible to the client.

Appendix B states 'We recorded every internal link found on every audited page: [N] links in total.' The placeholder '[N]' was never filled with the actual count from the audit data, leaving a raw template token in the client-facing deliverable.
findings.context:
## Appendix B: Link Inventory
We recorded every internal link found on every audited page: [N] links in total.

findings.message: The Priority 4 recommendation to 'Audit Open Graph and meta-description coverage across the audited set' names only a domain category without anchoring to any specific page, field gap, or count from the audit data. The Priority 4 block contains a score (49/100) but the individual recommendation bullet itself prescribes only a generic audit action with no data anchor identifying which pages lack which fields.
findings.context:
**What to change and why:**
- **Audit Open Graph and meta-description coverage across the audited set.** Where pages lack these fields, machines that rely on page-level metadata for content summarisation may fall back to arbitrary text, producing less accurate representations of dkd.de content in social and AI-driven surfaces.

findings.message: The Priority 4 recommendation to 'Add structured metadata for authorship and publication dates where content type warrants it' names only a domain category (authorship metadata) with no page URL, specific missing field name, or schema property anchoring it to this audit's findings. It could be copied verbatim into any web audit report.
findings.context: - **Add structured metadata for authorship and publication dates where content type warrants it.** Machines assessing content freshness and credibility use these signals; their absence reduces the confidence score machines assign to dkd.de content when ranking candidate sources for agent answers.

findings.message: The phrase 'leaves machines without structural context and forces them to rely on positional inference to determine meaning' is used twice in the report — once in the findings and once in the Div Soup section — as a rhetorical amplifier. While individually it describes a real technical consequence, the construction 'forces them to rely on positional inference' reads as passive-aggressive condemnation rather than neutral technical description, particularly given its exact repetition.
findings.context: On the audited contact page (https://www.dkd.de/de/kontakt), we recorded 26 of 48 divs as bare elements, a 54% ratio that leaves machines without structural context and forces them to rely on positional inference to determine meaning.

findings.message: The Pipeline Survivability table reports Truncation Risk as 'Fail' on 7/7 pages with 'Largest page: 232 KB. Threshold: 250 KB.' — meaning no page actually exceeds the 250 KB threshold. The data contradicts the Fail verdict and the accompanying prose ('7 page(s) exceed the 250 KB threshold'). This is an internal inconsistency that overstates the severity of the finding.
findings.context: | Truncation Risk | Fail | 7/7 | 7 page(s) exceed the 250 KB threshold. Agents with limited fetch windows may stop reading before reaching the main content. | Largest page: 232 KB. Threshold: 250 KB.

findings.message: The 'Full Optimization' phase in Next Steps is labelled 'Full machine readiness — every agent, search engine, and structured-data consumer can read, trust, and act on the site.' Claiming that completing P1–P5 delivers total machine readiness for every agent class and every structured-data consumer is unsupported by the audit data and reads as marketing copy rather than consultant prose.
findings.context: | Full Optimization | P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 (P1-P5) | Full machine readiness - every agent, search engine, and structured-data consumer can read, trust, and act on the site |

findings.message: The Inline Code Duplicates section identifies a JavaScript fragment beginning '(function(l,e,a,d,i,n,f,o){if(!l[i]){l.GlobalLeadinfoNamespace' — this is the Leadinfo analytics/tracking SDK — and a fragment beginning 'var _mtm = window._mtm' which is the Matomo Tag Manager loader. Both are injected by third-party vendor scripts, not authored in the site template. The recommendation prescribes moving each fragment to 'a shared external file' via template-level edits ('Move each duplicate fragment to a shared external file'), which is not a valid remediation path for vendor-injected scripts. Neither the Leadinfo nor the Matomo vendor origin is acknowledged, and no SDK-upgrade or DOM-observer path is described.
